name: Send appointment reminders and handle replies with Twilio and Claude

parameters.content:
## Send appointment reminders and handle replies with Twilio and Claude

**Who's it for**
Clinics, salons and service businesses losing revenue to no-shows.

**How it works**
Trigger: Hourly scan of upcoming appointments in the scheduling system; webhooks for new bookings, cancellations and inbound SMS replies.
1. Pull upcoming appointments
2. Decide the cadence and channel
3. Send the reminder
4. Understand replies
5. Book reschedules from real availability
6. Fill cancellations from the waitlist
7. Update the record and the desk
8. Report weekly
Every AI step is followed by a "Needs a person?" gate that parks low-confidence items instead of guessing.

**How to set up**
1. Open "Config (edit me)" and fill in the fields (names, approver, quiet hours, thresholds).
2. Add credentials to each service node.
3. Run once with test_mode on, read the output, then switch the trigger on.

**Requirements**
An Anthropic API key for the Claude nodes, plus Twilio, Scheduling system (Dentrix, Cliniko, Acuity, Calendly…) (or their equivalents — the nodes are standard and easy to swap).

**How to customize the workflow**
Set the reminder timing and the reschedule rules in the Config node; connect your scheduling system (Acuity, Calendly, Cliniko…). Keep the guardrail: Only patients with recorded consent for SMS or automated calls are messaged; opt-out words stop the sequence immediately.

Full blueprint with trigger, steps, guardrails and where the standard version stops: https://agentmelt.com/workflows/appointment-reminders-automation/

## Appointment Reminder Workflow

Starter template from agentmelt.com — configure before running:

1. Fill in "Config (edit me)" (name, approver, quiet hours; test_mode stays on for the first week).
2. Add credentials to every service node (Anthropic, mail, CRM, database…).
3. Replace placeholder URLs, queries and field mappings with yours.
4. Set the trigger: Hourly scan of upcoming appointments in the scheduling system; webhooks for new bookings, cancellations and inbound SMS replies.
5. Keep the gates: 'Needs a person?' after every AI step, 'Approved?' after the approval — wire their dead ends to a sheet or a channel.
6. Keep the guardrails:
   - Only patients with recorded consent for SMS or automated calls are messaged; opt-out words stop the sequence immediately.
   - Messages contain no clinical detail — appointment type, time and location only — to stay within HIPAA-safe messaging practice.
   - Reschedules are booked only into real availability; the agent never promises a slot it cannot see.
   - Ambiguous or emotional replies route to a person, with the thread.

Full blueprint and pricing: https://agentmelt.com/workflows/appointment-reminders-automation/
Want it built and run for you? $197/month · custom $2,000–4,000 one-time

## Steps

1. Schedule Trigger (hourly)
2. HTTP Request: Pull upcoming appointments
3. Code: Decide the cadence and channel
4. HTTP Request: Send the reminder
5. AI Agent: Understand replies
6. HTTP Request: Book reschedules from real availability
7. Loop Over Items: Fill cancellations from the waitlist
8. Google Sheets: Update the record and the desk
9. Schedule Trigger: Report weekly
10. Code: Report weekly

Every AI step is followed by "Needs a person?"; the write-back waits for "Approved?" where the blueprint has an approval step.

options.systemMessage:
You are the "Understand replies" step of the Appointment Reminder Workflow workflow run by Agentmelt.
Task: Free-text replies are classified — confirm, cancel, reschedule (with the proposed time extracted), question — and the agent drafts a short reply; ambiguous messages go to the front desk.

Rules:
- Only patients with recorded consent for SMS or automated calls are messaged; opt-out words stop the sequence immediately.
- Messages contain no clinical detail — appointment type, time and location only — to stay within HIPAA-safe messaging practice.
- Reschedules are booked only into real availability; the agent never promises a slot it cannot see.
- Ambiguous or emotional replies route to a person, with the thread.
- Answer only from the data provided in the input. If something is missing, say so in the output instead of guessing.
- If this step produces a message or a document, put the full text in `draft` (and a `subject` if it is an email); put a one-line summary in `summary`.
- Set `needs_human` true whenever you are unsure, the input is unusual, or a rule above applies; a person will look at it.
- Return valid JSON matching the output schema; no prose outside the JSON.

nodes.notes: True = the AI step was not sure or flagged the item → dead letter, a person looks. False = continue. Wire the dead letter to a Slack message or a sheet so nothing fails silently.

nodes.name: Needs a person: Understand replies
nodes.notes: Dead letter. Replace this no-op with a Slack message or a sheet row that carries the raw item and the reason — silent failures are the ones that cost.

parameters.notes: For reschedule requests, the workflow reads open slots for the same provider and type, offers the nearest three, and books the one the patient picks.
